source_block.parva: Drona Parva · fifteenth day · Drona-vadha upaparva
source_block.bori: BORI CE Drona Parva (Drona-vadha), Debroy translation vol. 6–7: Drona's slaughter on the fifteenth; Krishna's counsel; Bhima slays the elephant Ashvatthama (of Indravarman of Malava); Drona doubts and asks Yudhishthira; 'Ashvatthama is slain' aloud, 'the elephant' indistinctly; the chariot touches the earth; Drona casts aside arms and sits in yoga; Dhrishtadyumna beheads him while his soul has already ascended; Arjuna had cried to take him alive.
source_block.gita_press: Gita Press Gorakhpur Mahabharata (Hindi, Drona Parva, Drona-vadha): same sequence; 'ashvatthama hatah — naro va kunjaro va', with the last words drowned by conches and drums.
source_block.ganguli: K.M. Ganguli, Drona Parva §190–193 (vulgate): same sequence; car 'four fingers' breadth above the earth' touches the ground; Arjuna's reproach of Yudhishthira and Dhrishtadyumna follows (§196).
source_block.divergence: Vulgate (Ganguli / Gita Press) popular rendering has the word 'elephant' drowned by conches and drums; BORI CE says only that Yudhishthira spoke 'elephant' indistinctly. Chapter numbers differ between CE and vulgate. Arjuna's formal rebuke of Yudhishthira sits in the Narayanastra-mokshana section right after.
source_block.chosen: Gita Press + BORI/Debroy overlap: Yudhishthira mutters 'the elephant' indistinctly; conches are the battle's din (Krishna's conch on the plate) rather than a staged trick. Ganguli for English wording.
source_block.notes: Not TV. Comic-mythology only; no gore — beheading told in narration, shown as gold light (plate-still). Ashwatthama the son is never shown; the elephant is a beast. Krishna = Ep 09 look lock; Arjuna = Ep 09 face, cream-white dhoti, no gold armor/peacock (A4 direction). Yudhishthira Ep 14 canon = cream-white royal dhoti (plate-counsel/conch). Never attach Ep01 plate-wide-gold or any finished plate as an Imagine ref.
